name: FastOpenCV (fastcv kernels)
baseline: OpenCV 4.14.0 cv::resize (INTER_CUBIC, INTER_AREA) and cv::transform, stock build
workload: cv::resize INTER_CUBIC and INTER_AREA x4 on a 1080p image (README table heading says 8UC1), plus cv::transform on 32FC3 (colour matrix), stock OpenCV versus the fastcv drop-in kernel with the same cv::Mat API.
claimed_speedup: resize INTER_CUBIC 3.4 ms -> 0.8 ms (4.1x, bit-exact); resize INTER_AREA x4 0.92 ms -> 0.02-0.25 ms (3.5-18.7x, +/-1 on 0.2% of pixels); transform 32FC3 7.9 ms -> 0.74 ms (10.7x, bit-exact); pow 32F (gamma) 19-22x
compiler_and_flags: g++ (version not stated), fastcv built with -O3 -march=native -fPIC (scripts/build-fastcv.sh); OpenCV built by scripts/build-linux-opt.sh with AVX2 baseline plus AVX512_SKX dispatch, LTO, CUDA 13.3, TBB
hardware: AMD Zen 5 (AVX-512 + VBMI, 32 threads, exact SKU not stated) with NVIDIA RTX 4090, Arch Linux
tradeoffs: Drop-in kernels that need OpenCV headers plus an OpenCV build with the repo's patches for best results; -march=native build so the library is machine specific; requires AVX-512 VBMI for some kernels; Rust FFI crate included.
caveats: Benchmark source is public (bench/resize_cubic_bench.cpp) but the README table does not say whether 'stock OpenCV' is the repo's linux-stock control build or the optimised dispatch build, nor the exact CPU SKU or g++ version. Resize rows are for one 1080p image (README heading says 8UC1); no 3- or 4-channel resize numbers and no downscale ratios other than x4 for INTER_AREA, and the transform row is 32FC3 so mixes types. The README's own GPU table shows stock CPU resize 2x is already fast (0.014 ms). Very new repo with no third-party reproduction. Resize is only part of a 30-kernel library.
found_via: GitHub topic page https://github.com/topics/image-processing?l=c%2B%2B&q=simd (listing line 'Optimized OpenCV 4.14.0 builds + fastcv kernel library: 24 rewritten kernels, 2-74x speedups'), then README read

name: colortwist
baseline: Intel IPP ippiColorTwist (and a plain C reference loop)
workload: Colour twist (3x4 matrix times RGB triple) on a 2048x2048 RGB48 and RGB24 bitmap, MB/s, repeated 100 times by test/testcolortwist.cpp, outputs compared against the C and IPP results.
claimed_speedup: RGB48 on i7-8700K, MSVC 19.27: IPP 1720.98 MB/s vs AVX 3291.02, AVX2 4297.74, AVX3 5175.55 MB/s (about 3.0x IPP for AVX3); RGB24: IPP 892.93 MB/s vs AVX3 2966.55 MB/s (3.3x, derived from page data). Ryzen 7 4700U, MSVC: RGB48 IPP 1836.64 vs AVX3 5572.38 MB/s
compiler_and_flags: MSVC 19.27.29112, Intel icl 19.1.3.311 and gcc 10.2.0; per-file flags from lib/CMakeLists.txt (/arch:AVX2 on MSVC, -mfma -mavx2 and -msse4.1 on GCC/Clang); build type not stated
hardware: Intel Core i7-8700K @ 3.70GHz; AMD Ryzen 7 4700U; Raspberry Pi 3b/4 (NEON, compared to the C version only)
tradeoffs: Does one operation (colour matrix transform on RGB24/RGB48, plus RISC-V and NEON versions); not a general colour management engine; the IPP comparison is Windows-oriented and needs IPP to reproduce.
caveats: IPP numbers appear only in the Windows MSVC/icl tables (the gcc table has no IPP row). The README calls itself a finger exercise; the IPP baseline is a vendor library, not ImageMagick or stb. Release build type is not stated.
found_via: GitHub topic page https://github.com/topics/image-processing?l=c%2B%2B&q=simd (listing 'An exercise in SIMD-optimization'), then README and test/testcolortwist.cpp read

name: CompV
baseline: OpenCV (cv::resize bilinear; cvtColor CV_RGB2GRAY, CV_YUV2RGB_I420, CV_RGB2HSV)
workload: 10,000 iterations on a 1282x720 image of: RGB24 to grayscale, YUV420P to RGB24, RGB24 to HSV, and bilinear scaling to 1064x597, CompV (hand-written assembly, SSE/AVX, multithreaded) versus OpenCV.
claimed_speedup: RGB24->Gray 449 ms vs 3086 ms ('almost 7 times faster'); YUV420P->RGB24 968 ms vs 5919 ms ('6 times'); RGB24->HSV 2137 ms vs 15709 ms ('7 times'); bilinear scaling 1474 ms (mt, avx2) vs 4148 ms ('almost 3 times'), and 2645 ms (mt, plain c++) is still faster than OpenCV
hardware: Intel Core i7-4790K @ 4.00GHz (8 CPUs), Apple iMac15,1 running Windows 8 Pro 64-bit
stars_or_usage: 212 stars, 46 forks; code used in the vendor's commercial SDKs
tradeoffs: GPL-3.0 (copyleft, commercial use needs the vendor's licence); README says it is an R&D project with no documentation and is not intended for use by other companies; hand-written assembler and TBBMalloc/TCMalloc are part of the quoted results; large library with GPU back ends.
caveats: The only evidence is the committed result file, dated to a Windows 8 era machine; the OpenCV version, compiler and build flags are not stated and the benchmark driver was not located. The file itself notes CompV results use assembler plus TBBMalloc/TCMalloc. CompV single-thread AVX2 bilinear (5435 ms) is slower than OpenCV's multithreaded 4148 ms, and the bicubic scaling and bicubic rotation rows are marked 'Shame!!' (no CompV result). The README's headline 'up to 50 times faster than OpenCV' is not matched by any row of the result file (the largest ratio there is about 28x, on a feature matcher, and the colour and scaling rows are about 3-11x).
found_via: WebSearch 'FlatCV pure C image processing computer vision library benchmark faster than OpenCV' (result list), confirmed on GitHub topic page https://github.com/topics/computer-vision?l=c%2B%2B&q=than+opencv, then README and speed_compare file read

name: DeltaCV
baseline: OpenCV (cv::cvtColor RGB2GRAY and RGB2HSV on CPU, and OpenCV chains for fused colour-space plus threshold operations)
workload: CUDA RGB2GRAY and RGB2HSV on a 480x640 image (GTX 1070) versus OpenCV on an i5 7500 CPU; AVX2 fused colour-space plus segmentation functions (ycrcbWithSeg, inRange, weightedGrayWithSeg, grayBRWithSeg) on a 1024x1280 image versus the OpenCV equivalent.
claimed_speedup: GPU RGB2GRAY 0.008-0.010 ms vs 0.340-0.360 ms (README speed-up column says 3.4-45; ms columns imply about 34-45x, derived from page data); GPU RGB2HSV 0.150-0.200 ms vs 3.900-4.400 ms (19.5-29.3x); CPU AVX2 ycrcbWithSeg 0.88-0.90 ms vs 6.68-6.75 ms (7.4-7.6x), inRange 3.5-4.0x
compiler_and_flags: CPU part built with -mavx2 -march=haswell (compiler not stated)
hardware: GPU table: NVIDIA GTX 1070 8G versus OpenCV on Intel i5 7500; CPU SIMD table: CPU model not stated
tradeoffs: Small collection of hand-written kernels rather than a full library; CPU kernels are fused operations (colour conversion plus segmentation) so they are not drop-in replacements for single OpenCV calls; GPU path needs CUDA and the transfer cost is not stated.
caveats: GPU kernels are compared with CPU OpenCV, not with OpenCV CUDA or NPP; unclear whether host-device transfers are included; OpenCV version and flags not stated; SIMD table has no CPU model; the RGB2GRAY speed-up cell (3.4 - 45) is internally inconsistent with its timings. Repository last updated April 2019.
found_via: GitHub topic page https://github.com/topics/image-processing?l=c%2B%2B&q=high+performance (listing 'A high performance library for image processing'), then README read
